title: The Token Tax: Systematic Bias in Multilingual Tokenization
abstract: arXiv:2509.05486v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Tokenization inefficiency is associated with structural disadvantages for morphologically complex, low-resource languages, inflating compute resources and reducing accuracy. We evaluate 11 large language models (LLMs) on AfriMMLU (5 subjects; 16 African languages); for the 10 models whose fertility we could compute, higher token fertility is associated with lower accuracy: all 50 model--subject slopes are negative, 24 are significant at p<0.05, and 12 remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction. We further find that reasoning models (e.g., DeepSeek R1, o1) have the highest average accuracy and the smallest English-African gaps among the models evaluated. In terms of economics, a doubling in tokens results in quadrupled training cost and time, underscoring the "token tax" faced by many languages. translated_title: 代币税：多语言分词中的系统性偏差
translated_abstract: 分词效率低下给形态复杂、资源匮乏的语言带来了结构性劣势，导致计算资源消耗增加和准确率下降。我们在 AfriMMLU 数据集（5 个学科；16 种非洲语言）上评估了 11 个大语言模型（LLM）；在能够计算分词生育率的 10 个模型中，分词生育率越高与准确率越低相关：全部 50 个模型—学科斜率均为负值，其中 24 个在 p<0.05 水平上显著，12 个在错误发现率（FDR）校正后仍然显著。我们进一步发现，推理模型（如 DeepSeek R1、o1）在所评估的模型中具有最高的平均准确率和最小的英语—非洲语言差距。在经济方面，token 数量翻倍会导致训练成本和时间增至四倍，凸显了许多语言所面临的“代币税”。这些结果推动了形态感知分词、公平定价以及面向公平自然语言处理的多语言基准的发展。
tldr: 该论文通过对 11 个大语言模型在 16 种非洲语言上的评估，揭示了更高的分词生育率会系统性降低准确率并使训练成本翻两番，从而量化了低资源、形态复杂语言所承受的“代币税”偏见。
en_tdlr: Evaluating 11 LLMs on AfriMMLU, this paper demonstrates that higher token fertility systematically lowers accuracy and quadruples training costs, quantifying the "token tax" imposed on low-resource, morphologically complex languages.
